cards.text: A man calls at the gate for the old newspapers and goes away with none.
A courier boy rings at the next bungalow, waits, and rings again.
A scooter goes down the lane with something loose rattling in its mudguard.
The neighbour's gardener cuts back the hedge on the far side of the wall; the clippings come over in handfuls.
A church bell somewhere beyond the trees keeps going for a long time.
Rain drums on the tin roof of the servants' quarters and runs off the sill in a rope.
The lamps along the lane are still lit; the end of the road is gone in the grey.
The sun is a flat orange coin behind the haze, and the leaves on the verandah steps are furred with grit.
A dry wind turns the leaves over on the path and pushes a paper cup along it.
A row of retired men in white shoes walk the path at a pace, arguing about a cricket score.
A shopkeeper rattles up his shutter and sweeps the step into the gutter.
A handcart of oranges is pushed along the back of the market with a bell tied to its handle.
